distinct_character_theorem.character_family: q_sigma = tau^{z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma)} = exp((z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma)) log(tau))
distinct_character_theorem.multiplicity_distinction: N(T) counts zeros in 0 < Im(rho) < T WITH multiplicity, whereas the vertical-progression fiber argument requires a lower bound on N_dist(T), the number of DISTINCT complex zeros in 0 < Im(rho) < T. Because every simple zero has multiplicity 1, distinct simple critical-line zeros provide an unconditional lower bound N_dist(T) >= N_0^*(T) >= (0.4058 - o(1)) N(T) >> T log T (Bui, Conrey, and Young 2011, Acta Arith. 150, 35-64, Theorem 1.1 & Section 2.2, arXiv:1002.4127v2; Conrey 1989; Levinson 1974 / Heath-Brown 1979).
proof_steps: 1. Fix one nontrivial zero rho_0 = 1/2 + z_{rho_0}.
2. Suppose toward a contradiction that {q_{rho_0, sigma} : zeta(sigma) = 0, sigma != 1 - conj(rho_0)} takes only finitely many complex values {w_1, ..., w_M} in C^x.

3. Since exp(z log(tau)) = exp(z' log(tau)) iff z - z' in (2*pi*i / log(tau)) Z, each value w_j restricts Re(z_sigma) to a single value and Im(z_sigma) = gamma_sigma to a single vertical arithmetic progression gamma_0^{(j)} + (2*pi / log(tau)) Z.
4. A finite union of M vertical arithmetic progressions with spacing 2*pi / log(tau) contains at most M * (T * log(tau) / (2*pi) + O(1)) = O_M(T) distinct zeros sigma with 0 < Im(sigma) <= T.

5. By the unconditional simple critical-line zero density theorem of Bui, Conrey, and Young (2011, Acta Arith. 150, 35-64, Theorem 1.1, eq. (1.1), p. 1 & Section 2.2, p. 3, arXiv:1002.4127v2; see also Conrey 1989 and Levinson 1974 / Heath-Brown 1979), the number of simple critical-line zeros satisfies N_0^*(T) >= (0.4058 - o(1)) N(T). Since simple zeros have multiplicity 1, the number of DISTINCT zeros satisfies N_dist(T) >= N_0^*(T) >= (0.4058 - o(1)) (T/(2*pi)) log(T/(2*pi*e)) >> T log T, contradicting O_M(T).
6. Therefore {q_{rho_0, sigma}} contains infinitely many distinct complex numbers != 1.

finite_laurent_projector_status.laurent_root_bound: Multiplying P_N(q) by q^N gives a complex polynomial Q_{2N}(q) = q^N P_N(q) in C[q] of degree <= 2N. Since Q_{2N}(q) vanishes on infinitely many distinct complex values q_{rho_0, sigma} (in particular on at least 2N + 1 distinct complex values), Q_{2N} = 0 identically over C, forcing all c_K = 0 and P_N(1) = 0.

finite_differential_projector_status.distinct_exponent_argument: For fixed rho_0, the map sigma |-> lambda_{rho_0, sigma} = z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma) is injective on distinct complex zeros sigma. Since zeta(s) has infinitely many distinct zeros on the critical line (Hardy 1914; Titchmarsh 1986, Theorem 10.1; and quantitatively N_dist(T) >= N_0^*(T) >> T log T by Bui-Conrey-Young 2011), there are infinitely many distinct complex pair exponents lambda_{rho_0, sigma} != 0 without needing any vertical-progression quotient. A complex polynomial p in C[lambda] of degree <= M vanishing on more than M distinct complex points must satisfy p = 0 identically, forcing p(0) = 0.
finite_differential_projector_status.rational_filter_extension: For any finite rational filter R(lambda) = p(lambda)/q(lambda) analytic at lambda = 0 (so q(0) != 0 and R(0) = p(0)/q(0) != 0), vanishing on all nonstationary pair exponents lambda_{rho_0, sigma} outside the finite pole set of q still forces the polynomial numerator p(lambda) in C[lambda] to have infinitely many distinct complex roots, hence p = 0 and R = 0.

pontryagin_audit.single_zero_character_scope: For a single-zero character chi_z(K) = tau^{K z}, boundedness/unitarity on Z or R holds iff Re(z) = delta_rho = 0, which IS the Riemann Hypothesis for rho.
pontryagin_audit.pair_character_scope: For the sesquilinear common-shift pair character tau^{r(z_rho + conj(z_sigma))}, boundedness/unitarity for ALL pairs (rho, sigma)—and in particular for the diagonal pair sigma = rho where z_rho + conj(z_rho) = 2 delta_rho—holds iff every delta_rho = 0. Therefore, invoking Pontryagin character orthogonality or an invariant mean on Z or R to annihilate all nonstationary pair characters implicitly assumes delta_rho = 0.

On the real grade axis sin(theta) = 0, cos(theta) = +-1, so any off-critical diagonal pair with Re(lambda) = 2 delta_rho != 0 has growth rate +-2 delta_rho != 0. Since sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1, no fixed zero-independent angle theta can simultaneously make both families unitary.

critical_line_oscillation_zero_witness_a.explanation: On Re(z) = 0 (z = i*gamma) at t = 1, hat{Phi}_1^{(2)}(-i*gamma) = conj(hat{Phi}_1^{(2)}(i*gamma)), so hat{Psi}_1^+(i*gamma) = Re(hat{Phi}_1^{(2)}(i*gamma)) = |hat{Phi}_1^{(2)}(i*gamma)| cos(theta(gamma)), which vanishes whenever the Riemann-Siegel phase theta(gamma) = arg Gamma((1/2+i*gamma)/2) - (gamma/2) log(pi) crosses pi/2 + pi*Z.

inversion_even_state_status.unsymmetrized_vs_symmetrized_distinction: The raw state Phi_t^{(2)} = (D^2 - 1/16)^2 tilde{g}_t has centered Mellin transform hat{Phi}_t^{(2)}(z) = (1/32)(z^2 - 1/4)^2 t^{-z/2} pi^{-(1/2+z)/2} Gamma((1/2+z)/2), which is provably nonzero everywhere in the open strip -1/2 < Re(z) < 1/2 (0 < Re(s) < 1) because Gamma has no zeros and (z^2 - 1/4)^2 vanishes only at z = +-1/2. However, even at t = 1, tilde{g}_1(u) = exp(-pi u^2) is additive Fourier self-dual (F tilde{g}_1 = tilde{g}_1), NOT multiplicatively inversion-even under (I Psi)(u) = u^{-1} Psi(u^{-1}), because pi^{-(1/2+z)/2} Gamma((1/2+z)/2) != pi^{-(1/2-z)/2} Gamma((1/2-z)/2). For the symmetrized inversion-even state hat{Psi}_t^+(z) = (1/2)(hat{Phi}_t^{(2)}(z) + hat{Phi}_t^{(2)}(-z)), nonnegativity W_rho = m_rho^2 |hat{Psi}_t^+(z_rho)|^2 >= 0 is proved unconditionally, whereas hat{Psi}_1^+(i*gamma) = Re(hat{Phi}_1^{(2)}(i*gamma)) oscillates through zero along Re(z) = 0 as arg Gamma((1/2 + i*gamma)/2) - (gamma/2) log(pi) winds.
